partner_context.their_ambition: The MMDA has brought the Pasig River Ferry back to life — a free public service down the one corridor that runs straight through the heart of Metro Manila while EDSA and the bridges sit locked in some of the world's worst traffic. The ambition is a clean, reliable river spine that carries commuters east–west across the metro and anchors the rehabilitation of the Pasig itself.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission, foiling upgrade to a network the MMDA already runs every day. The same river stations — Guadalupe, Kalawaan, Maybunga, Sta. Ana, Lambingan, Pureza and on toward Intramuros — served by fast, near-silent, low-wake foiling ferries: more capacity on the busiest commuter reaches and no diesel wake on a river the city is working to bring back.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Metro Manila, Philippines · MMDA Pasig River Ferry
hero.title: Navier × Pasig River Ferry — the metro's river spine, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on the free Pasig River service: faster east–west crossings through the heart of Metro Manila, cleaner air, and real relief from some of the world's worst road congestion.
hero.what_we_do_together: The MMDA brings the Pasig River ferry network, the stations and the free public-service mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and certification path. Together we run the same river the metro depends on — faster, quieter and zero-emission — as the Pasig is cleaned and re-opened to the city.

why_now: The MMDA revived the Pasig River Ferry Service as a free public service and is expanding it station by station — toward 18 terminals — as the water spine of the Pasig River rehabilitation. The stations and ridership exist today; a foiling-electric layer is the fast, clean next step for the busiest commuter reaches.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the existing Pasig River service — the Makati and Pasig stations at Guadalupe, Kalawaan and Maybunga, the Manila midstream stations at Sta. Ana, Lambingan and Pureza, and the downtown terminals toward Intramuros — taking the high-frequency commuter reaches while conventional ferries keep heavier runs. Commuters step from bus and rail straight onto a foil down the river.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is proven in service and purpose-built for exactly this job: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (critical on a narrow, recovering urban river), near-silent, and zero-emission. It adds speed and clean capacity to a free public service on the one corridor that cuts straight through Metro Manila's gridlock.

proof_points.claim: The Pasig River Ferry is a live, free public service.
proof_points.evidence: MMDA revived the Pasig River Ferry Service; ~11–12 active stations across Manila, Mandaluyong, Makati and Pasig, with a plan toward 18 terminals.

proof_points.claim: The river itself is being brought back.
proof_points.evidence: The ferry is the water spine of the Pasig River rehabilitation / urban-development program.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.
The Philippines' net-zero pathway and Metro Manila's mandate to decongest EDSA and the metro's roads.

objections.concern: Can a foiling ferry work on a narrow, busy urban river?
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at the existing stations, flies above the chop for a smoother ride, and its low wake protects a narrow, recovering riverbank — an advantage on the Pasig, not a liability.

objections.concern: Is this affordable for a free public service?
objections.response: Foiling-electric is ~10x more efficient than a diesel planing hull, so fuel — the largest operating cost — falls sharply; the same public budget runs more frequent crossings.

objections.concern: Does this replace the ferries people rely on?
objections.response: No — it's a faster layer above them. Conventional ferries keep running underneath; the foiling fleet adds speed and zero-emission capacity on the busiest reaches.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path, aligned to Philippine maritime (MARINA) requirements.
the_ask.partner_brings: The Pasig River station map, the free public-service mandate, and the station-expansion plan already underway.
the_ask.next_step: Pick the first busy Pasig reach for a foiling-electric public pilot and align it with the MMDA's station-expansion plan.

close.body: The Pasig River Ferry is already carrying commuters for free through the heart of Metro Manila. Navier is how that service gets faster and cleaner on its busiest reaches — giving every rider a quick, quiet, zero-emission trip down the river, and giving one of the world's most congested metros real relief on the water.

end_state.headline: A zero-emission foiling layer across the Pasig River commuter spine.
end_state.addressable_footprint: The Pasig River Ferry network east–west through Metro Manila — Makati and Pasig upstream, the Manila midstream stations, and downtown toward Intramuros — re-platformed onto foiling-electric vessels.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II across the river network
steady_state.the_opportunity: A fast, zero-emission public river service for one of the world's most congested metropolitan cores.
